sources.entry: LeftHandy - Left-handed mouse and cursor support: mirrors system cursors so the tip points naturally and swaps left/right click in real time.

summary.one_liner: LeftHandy is a macOS menu bar app that mirrors system cursors and swaps left and right mouse clicks for left-handed use.
summary.what_it_does: LeftHandy runs in the macOS menu bar and flips the system cursors (arrow, pointer, resize handles, crosshair, and others) so the tip points naturally for left-handed users. It swaps left and right click in real time through a low-level event tap, without changing System Settings. The flipped cursors are reapplied after display reconfiguration, app switches, and wake from sleep. The dropdown offers an Active toggle, a Swap Mouse Buttons toggle, Start at Login, About, and Quit. A first-launch welcome flow asks for Accessibility permission and monitors its status. The app ships as a universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel and has no external dependencies.
use_cases: Using a mouse in the left hand on a Mac
Flipping cursor direction for left-handed use
Swapping left and right click on macOS
Keeping left-handed cursor settings across restarts and sleep
Avoiding changes in System Settings for mouse button order
how_to_run: Download the latest LeftHandy.dmg from the Releases page
Open the DMG and drag LeftHandy to Applications
Launch LeftHandy and grant Accessibility permission in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility
Toggle Active to flip cursors and Swap Mouse Buttons to swap clicks
To build from source: clone the repo, open LeftHandy.xcodeproj in Xcode 16+, and run the LeftHandy scheme
notable: Cursor flip mirrors all system cursors, not just the pointer
Button swap works through a low-level event tap without changing System Settings
Cursors are reapplied after display changes, app switches, and wake from sleep
Signed, notarized, and stapled releases as a universal binary
